Need + Passive infinitive and Need + verb+ing
Need + passive infinitive and need +verb+ing are two structures you use to talk about fixing problems.

You use these structures to imply that we don't know who will fix the problem, or that the person fixing the problem is not the focus of the sentence.

Subject + Need + Passive Infinitive

The manuscript needs to be looked at first.

The subject of the sentence is the thing that needs fixing/to be fixed.

Subject + Need + Verb + ing

That article needs proofreading.
Factual information needs to be verified before it is published.
Your work needs to be finished before you leave.
There are so many things that need to be considered when proofreading a manuscript.
Manuscripts need to be read under your breath to help identify pesky mistakes.
The time I spend at night working needs reconsidering.
Do any other manuscripts need proofreading before 9 a.m?

When you use a clause with verb + ing, there are some rules you need to keep in mind.
You can use a clause with a gerund (verb + ing) as the subject or the complement of a sentence.
After printing out the manuscript, you are better able to review it line by line.
Double-checking facts, figures, and proper names is essential.

As the subject:

When writing at speed, there can be a tendency to forget small words that don't impact the meaning of the sentence.

As the complement:

There can be a tendency to forget small words that don't impact the meaning of the sentence when writing at speed.

A complement is a group of words that give another word more meaning. You can use them after adjectives.

Other clauses with v-ing come after prepositions:

I can get that done quickly by organizing my time better.

There are so many things that need to be considered when proofreading. The boss wanted to know when I would have it finished. I asked if there was a deadline and she said, “I expect it on my desk by 9 a.m.” Having taken the early train to work since I started, today might be the day that I drive to the office. It will give me more time to finish proofreading. I suppose I should get cracking on this although the time I spend at night working needs reconsidering.

Here are the main areas I want to cover when reading over the manuscript:

Spotting too many problems at one time can leave a proofreader frustrated and overwhelmed. Focus on one type of problem at a time.
When writing at speed, there can be a tendency to forget small words that don't impact the meaning of the sentence. Some experts suggest that manuscripts need to be read under your breath to help identify pesky mistakes.
While reading through a text, you can concentrate on different areas like sentence structure, then word choice, then spelling, and finally, punctuation.
Sometimes sentences need trimming. Run-on sentences are not acceptable.
Double-checking facts, figures, and proper names is essential. Factual information needs to be verified before it is published.

Does the information need rearranging? Consider moving content up or down the page.
After printing out the manuscript, you are better able to review it line by line. It may help you catch errors that you previously missed.
A spellchecker can help you catch repeated words, reversed letters, and many other common errors.
Creating your own  checklist while proofreading can help you reflect on common mistakes and patterns.
